messages:
Aisha (devex): heads up — QA found weird import failures when using the JS SDK in a Next.js app-router server component running on the Edge runtime. stack traces show undefined default exports. Marco (eng-runtime): ugh, that usually smells like an ESM/CJS interop mismatch + package exports map. do you have a small repro? Aisha (devex): minimal repro attached inline: server component does `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` and then crashes. swapping to `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` works in dev but fails after build on Vercel Edge. Jun (eng-platform): Edge (V8) bundles + Next's SWC can rewrite imports. we recently changed the package exports to provide both `./edge` and `./node` entrypoints — maybe next's resolver picks the wrong one. Sam (eng): also check `type: module` + default export presence. If package.json exposes only named exports in the ESM build, CommonJS consumers using `require()` see `{ default: undefined }`. Aisha (devex): repro gist snippet: ``` // app/server-component.tsx import Redwood from 'redwood-inference' export default async function Page(){ const client = Redwood.createClient({ token: process.env.RW_TOKEN }) const r = await client.generate('hi') return 
{r.text}
} ``` Marco (eng-runtime): try using our explicit edge entrypoint in the short term: `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'` — that one is ESM-only and avoids CJS shims. also patch published yesterday adds `exports` entries. Aisha (devex): we tried that, still fails in prod only. error now shows `fetch is not a function` coming from our auth retry wrapper inside edge bundle. dev server had global fetch. Sam (eng): Next Edge runtime provides `fetch`, but Vercel's build step sometimes polyfills differently. Are you using the node-auth helper that calls globalThis.fetch during module init? that's a no-no for edge. Aisha (devex): yes — our token refresher does a synchronous call at module top-level for a cached token. moving to lazy init fixed it locally. can we document that server-only modules must avoid sync network calls at import time for Edge? Jun (eng-platform): good idea. action items: 1) add a clearer note in SDK docs about edge-safe entrypoints and top-level side-effects, 2) publish a small migration FAQ for Next.js app-router server vs client boundary, 3) patch the package.json exports/types to ensure consistent ESM typings for `./edge`. Marco (eng-runtime): on the typings piece — TS consumers were getting the wrong types for the `edge` build because `types` was only pointed at `dist/index.d.ts`. We'll publish separate `dist/edge.d.ts` and set `exports.{"./edge"}.types`. that should reduce confusion. Aisha (devex): for DX, can we add a runtime check that throws a helpful error when the SDK detects runtime=edge but a node-only import path was used? something like: `if (globalThis?.process?.versions?.node) { /* node */ } else { throw new Error('Use redwood-inference/edge in Edge runtimes — avoid top-level network calls') }` Sam (eng): I like it. implement a soft warning first so customers don't break immediately. CI-bot: deploy-preview for docs update is green :white_check_mark:. Marco (eng-runtime): final note: recommend examples in /examples/nextjs-app-router use explicit `use server` + `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'` in server actions and `use client` + `@redwood/inference-client` (client-only light wrapper) in client components. that pattern avoids accidental server-only module leakage. Aisha (devex): thanks all — I'll open a small PR with docs + a repro in examples and add a short bullet to the migration guide. keeping thread here for followups. :thumbsup:
